howTo: Enter the required pitch diameter D (mm) and the number of teeth Z. The tool calculates the raw module m = D / Z, then finds the nearest standard module from the ISO 54 / DIN 780 series.
Review the suggested standard module, the corrected pitch diameter, and the deviation percentage. A deviation above 2–3 % typically requires a design revision.
Check the undercut risk flag. For involute gears with a pressure angle of 20°, undercut is geometrically possible when Z < 17.
formula: m_raw = D / Z | m_std = nearest value from ISO series | D_std = m_std × Z | deviation = |D_std − D| / D × 100 %

examples.title: Spur gear design from pitch diameter
examples.description: A gearbox design calls for a pinion with a 60 mm pitch diameter and 20 teeth. Find the standard module.
notes: m = 60 / 20 = 3.000 — an exact match with the ISO standard series, so no deviation correction is needed.
Standard modules from ISO 54 preferred series: 0.5, 0.6, 0.8, 1, 1.25, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, 16, 20.

examples.title: Small gear with undercut risk
examples.description: A compact reducer needs Z = 14 teeth with a 28 mm pitch diameter. Assess module selection and undercut.
notes: Z = 14 < 17 triggers the undercut risk flag for a standard 20° pressure angle involute profile.
Mitigations: profile shift (addendum modification), increasing pressure angle to 25°, or increasing tooth count. Verify with tooth geometry software before production.

references.title: ISO 54
references.note: Cylindrical gears — ISO system of accuracy — Part 1: Definitions and allowable values of deviations relevant to corresponding flanks of gear teeth. The standard module series used in this tool.

references.title: DIN 780
references.note: Module series for gears. Equivalent to ISO 54 preferred module values, widely referenced in European mechanical engineering.

references.title: ISO 53
references.note: Cylindrical gears for general and heavy engineering — Standard basic rack tooth profile. Defines the 20° pressure angle reference geometry.

commonMistakes: Selecting a non-standard module (e.g. m = 2.8) — this requires custom tooling and significantly increases manufacturing cost.
Ignoring the undercut risk flag for small tooth counts and assuming a standard profile will still produce a valid tooth form.
Confusing pitch diameter (reference diameter) with tip diameter — the tip diameter is D_a = m × (Z + 2) for a standard tooth profile.
assumptions: Standard involute tooth profile with a 20° pressure angle, as defined by ISO 53.
No profile shift (addendum modification coefficient x = 0). Profile shift calculations require a separate gear design tool.
The undercut threshold of Z < 17 is approximate for a 20° standard pressure angle. The exact limit depends on the profile shift coefficient.
